name: splitting-schemes
title: Operator-splitting schemes for PDE/particle coupling: Jacobi (fvsolver), Gauss–Seidel, Strang
question:
The embedded vcell-fvsolver hard-codes one lagged (Jacobi-type) splitting. With the
coupling expressed as process-bigraph processes, can other splittings be used, and how
much accuracy do they buy at a given coupling interval?
hypothesis:
Jacobi and both Gauss–Seidel orderings are first order in the coupling interval τ.
Symmetric Strang splitting (half the PDE substeps, the particle step, the other half) is
second order in the mean dynamics and much more accurate at large τ.
description:
HybridCoupler composes the same FVReactionDiffusion and SmoldynHybrid engines and only
orders their substeps. Its jacobi scheme reproduces the two-process composite with
coupling="fvsolver" exactly (same seeds give identical counts; regression test in
tests/test_hybrid_cosim.py).

behavior_tests.name: jacobi-first-order
behavior_tests.description: Fitted order of the Jacobi (fvsolver) scheme.

provenance.note: Explicit lagged splitting is first order.

behavior_tests.name: strang-much-more-accurate
behavior_tests.description: Strang error / Jacobi error at the largest coupling interval (k = 32, τ = 0.16 s).

provenance.note: Symmetric splitting cancels the leading splitting error.

conclusion:
Results (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-03):
- **First-order schemes:** Jacobi (fvsolver) has order 1.23, Gauss–Seidel orders are
  1.01 and 1.08. At τ = 0.16 s their errors are about 0.021–0.023.
- **Strang:** the error stays within about 2× of the sampling floor (4–11·10⁻⁴) for every
  τ up to 0.16 s, 25× smaller than Jacobi at τ = 0.16 s. It is too close to the floor to
  fit an order; more seeds or larger τ would resolve it.
- **Consequence:** for this model, Strang splitting lets the particle side step about 32×
  less often than the PDE side at roughly the accuracy fvsolver's scheme reaches with
  k ≈ 1–2. That's a large potential speed-up for particle-dominated runs (A6).
  vcell-fvsolver's hybrid loop (SimTool.cpp) fixes one splitting order, so adopting
  Strang there would mean modifying the solver; here it is a coupler option.
